SMALL DETAILS. EVERYDAY DIFFERENCE.

Build once.
Test with less repetition.

The tools behind the workflow,
and what each one helps you do.

01 / REQUESTS

Make every request reusable.

Choose a method and URL, add query parameters, headers, authentication and a body, then save the request with its timeout settings. Reopen it when you need the same check again.

HTTP / HTTPSAuth & headerscURL import
02 / RESPONSES

Understand what came back.

See status, duration, headers and response content together. Format JSON or XML to make a payload easier to read, and revisit local history when you need an earlier result.

JSON / XMLStatus & timingLocal history
03 / ENVIRONMENTS

Change the target, keep the work.

Use variables such as {{base_url}} across your saved requests. Switch environments to reuse a collection with different endpoints or values, and mark sensitive variables as secrets.

Reusable variablesSecret valuesEnvironment switching
04 / TESTS & COLLECTIONS

Give “looks good” a clear check.

Save expectations for status, duration, response text, headers or JSON values. Run a collection to check requests together, with optional retries, delays and stop-on-failure.

Saved assertionsCollection runnerPass / fail results
05 / ORGANIZATION & TRANSFER

Keep your work easy to find.

Group related APIs into workspaces, collections and nested folders. Import and export Postman collections and environments to reuse your requests, folders and variables across tools. Environment exports leave secret values blank by default. Import or export supported OpenAPI files, or move local work with password-encrypted portable backups.

Postman import / exportCollections & environmentsOpenAPI import / exportEncrypted backups
06 / EXAMPLES & MOCKS

Keep building between releases.

Save example responses with a request and serve them through the local mock server. Give your frontend a predictable response while the real endpoint is still being built or changed.

Saved examplesLocal mock serverPredictable fixtures

A FEW GOOD QUESTIONS

A little clarity
before you start.

Is API Workbench really free?+

Free Local is always free to use, with the local features described on this page included. There is no trial countdown. The optional Buy Me a Coffee link appears after downloading and never gates an installer. Personal Sync and Collaboration are Coming soon.

Can I run a collection from my terminal?+

Yes. Choose Desktop + CLI, create your collections in the desktop app, then use apicollab list to find their IDs. Run a saved collection with apicollab run and optional environment, retry, delay or stop-on-failure flags.

Can I work offline?+

No account or API Workbench server is required for Free Local. Edit and organize saved work, inspect history and test reachable local APIs without our services. Requests to internet endpoints still require a network connection.

How is my local data protected?+

Sensitive saved fields use Windows user-scoped protection, macOS Keychain, or Linux Secret Service, depending on your OS. Keep your OS keyring available and unlocked. Use password-encrypted portable backups to move work between computers or OS accounts; a raw database copy does not transfer its encryption key.

Which installer should I choose?+

Start with Desktop for a visual workflow, or choose Desktop + CLI for terminal collection runs too. Choose Apple Silicon for an M-series Mac, Intel for an Intel Mac, and the matching x64 or ARM64 architecture on Linux. macOS downloads here use .pkg; Linux .deb files target compatible Ubuntu/Debian-family desktops.

How do imports, backups and the CLI fit together?+

Supported Postman/OpenAPI imports bring request definitions into your local workspace. Portable backups transfer supported local work in an encrypted file. The CLI lists and runs the desktop’s saved collections under the same OS account. Format coverage varies, so review import results for unsupported items.

What should I know about the beta?+

These installers are unsigned evaluation builds, shipped without saved workspaces or sign-ins. macOS/Linux native jobs passed 344 tests per target, plus package, CLI, keyring and GUI-startup checks. Full manual UI coverage and existing dependency-advisory fixes remain outstanding. Back up important work before testing updates. Personal Sync and Collaboration are unavailable.
